page: OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an x86_64 Intel processor based on the Haswell architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets. The instance is provisioned with 60.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core, and includes 400 GB of local SSD storage alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core and memory performance, contrasted by weaker single-core capabilities. The server achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 15,173.66 and a PassMark CPU score of 18,774.29, placing it in the middle tier of performance. Single-core performance is limited, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,067.12 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.52 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth is solid at 1,353.9 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 45.81 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 20.8 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated core allocation and balanced resource profile, the b2-60 offers a stable environment for multi-threaded workloads that do not require modern AVX-512 instructions. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 14.61 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a Redis SET performance of 19.76 million operations per second. The inclusion of 400 GB of local SSD storage and a dedicated CPU model provides predictable performance for general-purpose applications, multi-threaded data processing, and medium-scale database hosting without the overhead of shared-core resource contention.
description: The OVHcloud b2-60 is a general-purpose server instance configured with 16 dedicated physical x86_64 Intel cores running at 2.0 GHz, 60.0 GB of RAM, and 400 GB of local SSD storage. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance delivers balanced resource density with 3.75 GB of memory per core and a 1 Gbps baseline network speed. Benchmark data shows average multi-core performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 18,774.29 and a Redis SET throughput of 19.76 million operations per second, though single-core performance and large-block memory write speeds are relatively weak. Lacking AVX-512 support, the b2-60 is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, and medium-scale database operations where dedicated CPU resources and local SSD storage are required.
